texts.preamble: Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Kabc020422342024 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.4969/2024
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 24-05-2024 at about 11:45 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in a Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ- 1468, from Kyasamballi village towards Balaganatham village. At that time, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, the driver of said Tata Sumo namely Srinivasulu Reddy drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side tree. Due to the said impact, the petitioner got stuck inside the vehicle and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to PES Hospital, Kuppam, wherein she took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident she was working as tailor and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, she has become permanently disabled and thereby lost her earning capacity. The Ramakuppam Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tata Sumo for the offence punishable under Section 337 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement. Whereas, the respondent No.1 did not choose to appear and remained absent. Hence, the respondent No.1 is placed as ex-parte. 4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of Private Car package policy bearing No.0516033123P116864129 in respect of Tata Sumo bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 and it was valid from 17-03-2024 to 16-03-2025. Further it is contended that, the driver of the Tata Sumo vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-01-MJ-1468 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the same, as on the date of accident. The respondent No.1/owner of said vehicle being aware of the same has consciously allowed such person to drive his vehicle and thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy. Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.1, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160442603/ 2 Act.
texts.arguments: Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1/owner of the Tata Sumo had allowed or permitted his driver to drive the said vehicle in the public place without a valid fitness certificate. As such, the respondent No.1 has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and had acted in contravention of the Motor Vehicle Act 1988. Further it is contended that, the said accident has occurred due to contributory negligence of the petitioner. The accident having occurred at around 11.45 p.m., during the night hours, on a busy road, near Green Valley School, Rajupeta Village, Ramakuppam Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh. The petitioner had not taken reasonable care for the safety of herself, as well as the driver of the vehicle. The act of the petitioner in having taken the risk of engaging the driver in conversion, has led him to jump the vehicle and it has resulted in the accident. The petitioner is liable for contributory negligence for not less than 75% and she is "author of her own wrong". Hence, the compensation if any awarded to the petitioner is to be reduced by 75% having contributed to the accident. Further, it has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from her mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of her evidence or which Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160442603/ 4 goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to her own negligence or there was any contributory negligence on her part, in the cause of accident. 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 16. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone Jagadeeswari C vs Harish A on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160442603/ 5 of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." 21. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 21 years is 18. Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,98,000 X 12/100 X 18 = Rs.4,27,680/-. 22. Medical expenses: The petitioner has deposed that, she has incurred expenses of Rs.50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, food & nourishment, attendant charges and other incidental charge. In order to prove the same, she has produced 9 medical bills, as per Ex.P.14. All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.5,118/- towards medical expenses.
